Ultimately from Latin rubrica.

parole.significato: festival/ritual game performed in the Pentecost week

From Latin sāpō (genitive singular sāpōnis), through the intermediate of Byzantine Greek σαπούνιον (sapoúnion). Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ.
Borrowed from Latin satira.

parole.significato: sect (religious group professing beliefs outside the accepted norm)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin secta. First attested in 1843.

Ultimately from Latin senātor.

parole.significato: September (the ninth month of the Gregorian calendar, following August and preceding October, containing the southward…
parole.testo: Ultimately from Latin September.

parole.significato: sine (ratio between the length of an opposite side to the length of the hypotenuse in a right-angle triangle)
parole.testo: Scientific term, ultimately from Latin sinus (“pocket, bosom”).

Formally formed from тексти́л (tekstíl, “textile”) + -ен (-en), reflecting Latin textīlis (“woven”). Objectively, borrowed from some Western language or from Russian.
Scientific term ultimately from Latin temperātūra.

parole.significato: tapeworm, taenia (parasitic flatworm of family Taeniidae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin taenia (“tape”), called so due to the oblong shape of the worm.

parole.significato: term (word or phrase, especially one from a specialised area of knowledge)
parole.testo: Ultimately from Latin terminus.
Transliteration of the taxonomic name Termitidae, from the plural stem of Latin termes (“woodworm”).

Borrowed from Latin traditio.

parole.significato: transformation, change, conversion (a process or result of changing something substantially in form, structure, charact…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin transformātiō (“transformation, change of form”).

parole.significato: podium, platform, rostrum, tribune (place, usually elevated, from which a speaker addresses an audience)

parole.significato: February (the short month following January and preceding March in the Roman, Julian, and Gregorian calendars, used in…

parole.significato: cholera (any of several acute infectious diseases of humans and domestic animals, caused by certain strains of the Vibr…

parole.significato: honorarium, fee, royalty (compensation, such as a salary, for professional services)
parole.testo: Derived from Latin honorarium, from honōrārius.

Internationalism; compare French chronologie, German Chronologie, Russian хроноло́гия (xronológija) ultimately from New Latin chronologia, from Ancient Greek χρονολογία (khronología).
Scientific term, ultimately from Latin humus (“ground, earth”). Akin to the native Bulgarian земя́ (zemjá, “earth”).

parole.significato: censorship (the use of state or group power to control freedom of expression or press, such as passing laws to prevent…

parole.significato: part of speech (linguistic category of a word or group of words)

parole.significato: July (the seventh month of the Gregorian calendar, following June and preceding August)

parole.significato: January (the first month of the Gregorian calendar, following the December of the previous year and preceding February)
